sources.name: Clarity Elections ENR (Civix/Scytl/SOE) - county/state hosted
sources.latency: Jurisdiction-controlled upload cadence; typically minutes to tens of minutes on election night (not verified live; no official doc)
sources.granularity: County or state; precinct via detailxml.zip in most but not all jurisdictions
sources.verified_live: PARTIAL. Root results.enr.clarityelections.com returns 200 (gzip HTML, 368 bytes). /NY/Dutchess/ = 404, /NY/Dutchess/current_ver.txt = 404 (Dutchess is NOT on Clarity). /GA/, /NC/, /NY/ return 403 (bot filter/directory listing blocked). I did not find a live election ID to confirm JSON, so JSON/XML paths are UNVERIFIED against a live site today.
sources.notes: Format: JSON summary (json/en/summary.json; Firecrawl sample suggests json/details.json on some versions), zipped detail XML (also CSV/XLS in the zip). Auth: none, but 403s on directory roots. Undocumented/unofficial: no published schema, per third-party cgorski.github.io page and the Firecrawl provider page. electionID is numeric and unpredictable; no central index, so discovery means crawling county BOE sites. Old results get removed. current_ver.txt pattern (read it for the newest version number, then fetch /{id}/{ver}/...) is claimed by Firecrawl only; I did not confirm it. Parsing libs: python 'clarify' (ghing/clarify), 'elex-clarity'. About 1,000+ jurisdictions in about 30 states per third-party estimate.

sources.name: North Carolina State Board of Elections - ENRS bulk files on S3
sources.latency: Files are refreshed in place during the night (NC claims frequent refreshes; exact interval not verified). results_pct_20261103.zip showed LastModified 2026-10-05 at my probe (about 7:20pm ET, before NC polls closed at 7:30pm), so it is still a placeholder and I could not observe a live update.
sources.granularity: Precinct (results_pct zip = precinct-level results for all contests, statewide) plus county-level absentee/voter_stats files
sources.verified_live: YES. The S3 bucket listing returns 200 XML. The ENRS/2026_11_03/ folder exists and contains absentee_*.zip/csv (updated 2026-11-03 09:20-10:36 UTC), polling_place_20261103.csv, provisional_20261103.txt, voter_stats_20261103.zip, results_pct_20261103.zip. Layout docs are at ENRS/layout_*.txt and ENRS/ReadMe_PUBLIC_DATA.txt.
sources.notes: Plain HTTP GET, S3 object listing, no key. Poll the object's ETag or Last-Modified with a HEAD request. Folder pattern is ENRS/YYYY_MM_DD/. The er.ncsbe.gov viewer links to the same downloads. Best-documented official statewide bulk feed I found. Official.
sources.official: Yes (official, but not a versioned API)

sources.name: Georgia SOS results (results.sos.ga.gov, Angular SPA)
sources.latency: Public file has Cache-Control public, max-age=60, so the CDN caches for 60 seconds at most; the underlying publish cadence is not verified
sources.granularity: Statewide, county, and precinct-level in the export JSON (32 MB for 2024)
sources.verified_live: PARTIAL. SPA page /elections/2026NovemberGeneral = 200 HTML. The 2024 export https://results.sos.ga.gov/cdn/results/Georgia/export-2024NovGen.json = 200, 33,718,327 bytes, last-modified 2025-01-30, max-age=60. My guessed 2026 IDs (2026NovGen, 2026General, 2026NovemberGeneral, 2026JuneGeneralPrimary) all returned 404, so I have NOT found the 2026 election ID. Find it from the SPA's network requests (XHR).
sources.notes: Format JSON. Pattern is a CDN export-{ID}.json (the 2024 ID was 2024NovGen). This is an undocumented feed behind the official site. Georgia moved off Clarity to this newer platform (the SPA-style ENR). Browser devtools or Playwright on the SPA is the quickest way to get the exact 2026 ID.

summary:
Bottom line from the vendor/state-feed slice. No vendor offers a documented, supported real-time API. What exists is a mix of undocumented JSON/XML behind official sites and bulk file drops.

Confirmed live by curl:
- North Carolina's S3 bucket (dl.ncsbe.gov/ENRS/2026_11_03/) responds and is the cleanest official statewide bulk feed. It is open, unauthenticated, precinct-level, with a results_pct zip. The results zip still showed a 2026-10-05 timestamp at my probe, about 7:20pm ET before NC polls closed, so I have not seen it update live.
- Georgia's CDN export pattern works (the 2024 export is 200, 32 MB, precinct-level JSON, max-age=60). I could not find the 2026 election ID; it needs the SPA's network calls.
- Clarity's root responds, but I could not find a live instance to confirm the JSON or XML paths. Clarity URLs need a numeric election ID that is unpredictable and has no central index. Everything I say about /json/en/summary.json, reports/detailxml.zip and current_ver.txt comes from third-party pages (cgorski.github.io, Firecrawl), not from my own probing.

Dutchess County: the BOE site (elections.dutchessny.gov) is a WordPress site with PDF/HTML results and a few old CSV/XLS files. It is NOT on Clarity (404). I found no API, and the board says results post slowly through the night, with absentees later. Plan on scraping its unofficial-results HTML page once the 2026 general page appears (I did not see it yet), or ask the BOE for CSV. I did not identify its vendor.

Blocked to curl (403 or bot challenge, so inconclusive, NOT proof of no API): NY State ENR (Cloudflare), PA (Imperva/Incapsula), TX, AZ, MO, IA. OH and MI did not connect. A headless browser (Playwright) would likely get through and let you read the XHR calls.

Not covered or not verified: KnowInk, Hart, ElectionStats, VR Systems, Tenex, Arcadia and Enhanced Voting were not researched with evidence. California has a documented JSON API (PDF found, not called). Washington has per-date CSV/XML export pages, but I could not find the 2026 one (404 on the guesses). Florida has pages reachable but no file endpoints confirmed.

Practical recommendation from this slice: a dashboard built on NC's S3 files, Georgia's CDN JSON, CA's JSON API, and Playwright-assisted discovery for the big blocked states is feasible. For anything truly real-time or national, an AP-type aggregator is probably the real option; that was outside my slice. County-level coverage for Dutchess will be slow and manual regardless of feed choice.
